# Scene encoders: transformers and sequence models

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">Seed-based · 5 methods</span><code class="gp-chip">--set backbone=</code><span class="gp-chip">16 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

These encoders attend over points, voxels, octree nodes or point patches: the Point Transformer
line (V1 to V3, with Sonata, Concerto and Utonia weights), LitePT, Volt, OctFormer, and the
point-patch tokens of PointViT, PointMamba and Uni3D. What all scene encoders share is on the
[overview](scene_encoders.md).

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

=== "GraspNet-baseline"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o graspnet-baseline_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list backbone
    ```

=== "GSNet"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o gsnet_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

=== "Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o scale-balanced-grasp_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list backbone
    ```

=== "EconomicGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o economicgrasp_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

=== "FineGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=ptv3 -o finegrasp_ptv3.yaml
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [GraspNet-baseline](../methods/graspnet_baseline.md#backbone) · [GSNet](../methods/gsnet.md#backbone) · [Scale-Balanced-Grasp](../methods/scale_balanced_grasp.md#backbone) · [EconomicGrasp](../methods/economicgrasp.md#backbone) · [FineGrasp](../methods/finegrasp.md#backbone).

<!-- method-options:end -->

    - **Runs**: out of the methods the option is a swap under, those under which its probe trained on real frames without error. A method that ships the option is named *own* and not counted; a method still undecided is counted and named. Measured on 20 training iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, one run per cell; nothing was measured on GraspClutter6D or on Kinect frames.
    - **Trains like shipped**: out of the methods under which the swap ran, those under which every comparable loss term ended within the method's tolerance of the component it ships, with nothing rising; a method left out is named with why. Measured on 250 iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, at a constant learning rate (FineGrasp: its own warm-up), beside the method as shipped trained the same way twice.

## Choosing

- **Serialised voxels:** `ptv3` and `litept` run on the 5 mm grid of the sparse encoders and
  come with released weights (`ptv3-scannet200`, `ptv3-ppt`, `litept-structured3d`; the Sonata
  weights are non-commercial).
- **The unit of length** is a setting of every encoder here: `grid_sizes` of
  `point-transformer-v2`, `grid_size × kernel_size` (the token edge) of `volt`, `voxel_size` of
  `octformer`; `point-transformer-v1` sub-samples by ratio and has none.
- **Point-patch tokens** (`point-vit`, `point-mamba`, `uni3d`) were designed for single objects;
  their tokens become the seeds, and `num_group` must equal the seeds of the method.
- **Attention cost:** `point-vit` attends globally (quadratic in the tokens), `point-mamba` is
  linear but runs on CUDA only.
- **The encoders checked against their authors' code** (PTv3, its Sonata and Utonia variants,
  LitePT) are on [Encoders checked against their authors' code](../model_zoo_backbones.md).

## Details

??? note "The settings that matter"

    **Point Transformer V2**: `grid_sizes` is the cell edge of the four poolings, in metres; the
    class defaults are for rooms, the preset divides the ScanNet values by 4.

    ```yaml
    model:
      backbone:
        type: PointTransformerV2
        grid_sizes: [0.015, 0.0375, 0.09375, 0.234375]   # metres
    ```

    **Volt**: `grid_size × kernel_size` is the edge of a token (2.5 cm in the preset); smaller
    tokens resolve finer geometry and cost quadratically more attention. `embed_dim / num_heads`
    must be 64. The authors state that Volt overfits without their training recipe (strong
    augmentation, distillation, EMA), which is not part of this toolbox.

    **OctFormer** (extra `ocnn`): `voxel_size` is the edge of an octree leaf; a frame must fit a
    cube of `voxel_size * 2**octree_depth`; `patch_size` octree nodes form one attention group.

    **PointViT, PointMamba, Uni3D** (extras `mamba-ssm` for PointMamba, `timm` for Uni3D):

    ```yaml
    model:
      backbone:
        type: PointViT                 # or PointMamba, or Uni3D
        num_group: 1024                # tokens per cloud = points with features = seeds
        group_size: 32                 # nearest points per token (Uni3D: 64)
        coord_scale: 2.0               # metres -> the unit-sphere scale of the object models
    ```

    **PTv3 and LitePT** take the sparse grid (`grid_size`) and, with `pretrained:`, a release by
    name (below). `ptv3-encoder` sets `enc_mode: true`: no decoder, the encoder stages
    concatenated on every voxel. `ptv3-ppt` holds one set of normalisation layers per training
    dataset; `pretrained_condition` picks one. Other files of the same releases (the larger PPT
    model, the later Sonata file, the large Concerto model, the larger LitePT models) have the
    same layout and are expected to load the same way; they were not downloaded, so pass such a
    file as a path.

??? note "Released weights for the point-patch encoders and Volt"

    These load through `tools/convert_encoder_checkpoint.py`, which reads the config you composed
    and writes the keys where the encoder sits:

    ```bash
    python -m tools.convert_encoder_checkpoint pretrain.pth point-mae.pth \
        --config <composed config>
    grasppanda train <composed config> \
        --opts runtime.load_from=point-mae.pth runtime.allow_weight_mismatch=true
    ```

    | Uni3D [`uni3d-ti/model.pt`](https://huggingface.co/BAAI/Uni3D/resolve/main/modelzoo/uni3d-ti/model.pt) | 13 | `Uni3D` | `timm_model: eva02_tiny_patch14_224` | object collections with colour, aligned with CLIP | code MIT; the model card states none | `6ff7e821e6997cb8` |
    | Uni3D [`uni3d-s/model.pt`](https://huggingface.co/BAAI/Uni3D/resolve/main/modelzoo/uni3d-s/model.pt) | 46 | `Uni3D` | the preset's | the same | the same | `9a6342fda2245f00` |
    | Volt-S [`joint_training_small`](https://huggingface.co/KadirYilmaz/Volt/resolve/main/Volt_experiments/joint_training_small/scannet/model/model_last.pth) | 381 | `Volt` | `in_channels: 6`, `grid_size: 0.02`, or `--fresh tokenizer.proj` with the preset | ScanNet, ScanNet200, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes, with distillation | MIT | `2ce43d64b17999fa` |

    </div>

    The checksums are those of the files as downloaded on 2026-10-13. All but Volt were trained
    on single objects scaled to the unit sphere: on a metric scene they are an initialisation of
    the transformer, not a feature extractor. With other encoder sizes nothing is written, and
    the tool names the option to change.

??? warning "Pitfalls met while building this"

    - **`mamba-ssm` on PyPI is a source build.** Prebuilt wheels per torch, CUDA and Python are on
      its [releases page](https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba/releases).
    - **`import mamba_ssm` compiles a Triton helper** and fails with `cannot find -lcuda` when the
      machine has `libcuda.so.1` but no `libcuda.so`: point `TRITON_LIBCUDA_PATH` at a directory
      with a link of that name.
    - **`PointMamba` has no CPU path**; on the CPU it says so.
    - **`ocnn` runs its convolutions on Triton kernels by default**, which did not compile here;
      `OctFormer` sets ocnn's pure-PyTorch path (`conv_method: block_gemm`).
    - **OctFormer's features depend on the batch**: attention groups are counts of z-ordered nodes
      of the whole batch, as in the reference.
    - **The default Concerto files are not the paper's Concerto.** The model card calls them
      pre-release Utonia models; the paper's model is `concerto-base-origin`.
    - **Object checkpoints use other sizes.** MaskPoint's ShapeNet file has the Point-BERT layout
      (`token_dim: 256`); its ScanNet file is a 3DETR encoder and does not fit `PointViT`.

??? note "Not wrapped"

    | Candidate | Why not |
    |---|---|
    | Swin3D | built on MinkowskiEngine plus its own CUDA package, neither a dependency here. |
    | Superpoint Transformer / EZ-SP | consumes a superpoint partition computed outside the network. |
    | Mamba3D, Point Cloud Mamba | no licence file. |
    | PointGPT | its blocks differ from `PointViT`'s, so its checkpoints need a second block type. |
    | ReCon, ACT, PCP-MAE, Point-JEPA, Point-BERT's own file | checkpoints behind links that were not downloaded; nothing is claimed. |
    | Point-M2AE | a hierarchical encoder, not the shared single-scale layout. |
    | Point-MoE, D-DITR, LAM3C weights for PTv3 | a mixture-of-experts block (Point-MoE); AGPL-3.0 (D-DITR) and non-commercial (LAM3C) weights, not downloaded. |
